title: SynBench: A Benchmark for Differentially Private Text Generation
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: Datasets that overlap more with pre-training data get higher synthetic quality and more membership leakage, so utility and privacy trade off.
layout: 2 panels: left 3+3 box grid with arrows, right scatter plot
description: The figure has two panels. The left panel is titled 'SynBench: Framework'. It shows a top row of three hand-drawn-style boxes joined by gray arrows: 1. Specialist Data (blue, 9 Domain Datasets), 2. DP-Generation (green, Privacy Budget ε), 3. Systematic Audit (purple, Black-box Auditing). Below it, 'Key Scientific Findings' has three boxes: No Free Lunch (orange), DP Guarantees Gaps (red, with an X icon) and Vulnerability of Outliers (teal). Each box has a small icon and a short caption. The right panel is a scatter plot of Mauve (y-axis) against log10(leakage percentage + 1) (x-axis). Blue circles show Mauve and red squares show AUC, one pair per dataset. The dataset names are Psytar, HoC, DMSAFN, Lc37Fnd, Eurlex, N2C2'08 and AsyLax. Dashed blue and red upward trend lines show that both quality and MIA signal rise with overlap. The eye goes first to the colorful boxes, then to the trend lines.
caption: No free lunch. Across datasets, higher estimated pre-training overlap goes with higher synthetic quality and MIA AUC (MAUVE; Spearman $\rho = 0.76$, $p = 0.04$).
abstract: Synthetic text generation with Differential Privacy (DP) guarantees emerges as a principled approach that can enable the sharing of sensitive datasets across institutional and regulatory boundaries, while bounding the risks of re-identification and membership inference. LLM-based methods deliver promising results; however, comparisons are exacerbated by differing evaluation setups and "private" datasets, potential pre-training contamination is not considered and guarantees are not verified with DP audits. To advance this field, we introduce a unified evaluation framework with standardised utility and fidelity metrics and privacy audits, encompassing nine curated datasets that capture domain-specific complexities such as technical jargon, long-context dependencies, and specialised document structures. In a large-scale empirical study, we benchmark LLM-based state-of-the-art DP text generators of varying sizes (between 1--8B). Our results indicate that DP synthetic text generation remains an unsolved challenge, with quality deteriorating more as the private datasets deviate further from the generators' pre-training corpora. Our analyses suggest that synthetic data quality may be overestimated when LLMs have been pre-trained---without DP---on portions of the "private" data to be generated, and our membership inference (MIA) auditing setup for synthetic text reveals measurable membership signals even under tight privacy budgets. Finally, we note that under the "public pre-training, private generation" paradigm, the nominal $(\varepsilon,Î´)$ guarantee does not account for exposure during pre-training, motivating contamination-aware evaluation of DP synthetic text generation. Code and data splits: https://github.com/ImperialGlobalSingapore/synbench
